ADR_O_WIDTH.note: Modular address width. Higher boundary is specific to the address width of the core; lower boundary is determined by the data port size and granularity. For example, on a 32-bit data port with BYTE granularity, [ADR_O(n..2)].

DAT_WIDTH.note: Port size — MUST be one of 8/16/32/64-bit per RULE 2.15 item 7.

GRANULARITY.note: Smallest unit a port can transfer; MUST be 8/16/32/64-bit per RULE 2.15 item 8.

SEL_WIDTH.note: Each [SEL_O(n)] qualifies one byte-lane of [DAT_I()]/[DAT_O()] per Section 3.5.

MAX_OPERAND_SIZE.note: MUST be 8/16/32/64-bit per RULE 2.15 item 9; if unknown, the maximum operand size equals the granularity.

CTI_O_WIDTH.note: Cycle Type Identifier Address Tag (Registered Feedback only).

BTE_O_WIDTH.note: Burst Type Extension Address Tag (Registered Feedback incrementing burst only).

TGA_WIDTH.note: User-defined width; declared per IP core.

TGD_WIDTH.note: User-defined width; declared per IP core.

TGC_WIDTH.note: User-defined width; declared per IP core.

data_organization_8bit_port.BYTE_granularity: Single 8-bit BYTE per transfer; BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN identical at this width (RULE 2.15 item 10 note).

key_constants_for_RTL_authoring.wishbone_handshake_rule: Standard: ACK_O/ERR_O/RTY_O generated from logical AND of CYC_I AND STB_I

default_signal_values_when_omitted.ACK_O: 0 (LOW) when no STB_I or CYC_I — also when SLAVE inserting wait state
default_signal_values_when_omitted.ERR_O: 0 (LOW) — RULE 3.45 at most one of ACK/ERR/RTY at any time
default_signal_values_when_omitted.RTY_O: 0 (LOW) — RULE 3.45 at most one of ACK/ERR/RTY at any time
default_signal_values_when_omitted.CTI_O: 3'b000 (Classic cycle) if absent at the MASTER, or the SLAVE assumes Classic if it does not implement CTI_I (RULE 4.10, PERMISSION 4.10 default 000)
default_signal_values_when_omitted.BTE_O: 2'b00 (Linear) when CTI_O does not indicate incrementing burst
default_signal_values_when_omitted.WE_O_idle: Don't-care during IDLE (qualified by STB_O per RULE 3.60)

evidence.quote: The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the port size: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit or 64-bit. The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the port granularity: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit or 64-bit. The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the maximum operand size: 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit or 64-bit. If the maximum operand size is unknown, then the maximum operand size shall be the same as the granularity. The WISHBONE DATASHEET MUST indicate the data transfer ordering. The ordering MUST be indicated as BIG ENDIAN or LITTLE ENDIAN. When the port size equals the granularity, then the interface shall be specified as BIG/LITTLE ENDIAN.
RULE 3.95: Data organization on 64-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-18 (BYTE / WORD / DWORD / QWORD granularity, BIG and LITTLE ENDIAN tables).
RULE 3.100: Data organization on 32-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-19.
RULE 3.105: Data organization on 16-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-20.
RULE 3.1010: Data organization on 8-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-21.

CTI_O(2:0) Cycle Type Identifiers: 000 Classic, 001 Constant address burst, 010 Incrementing burst, 011-110 Reserved, 111 End-of-Burst. BTE_IO(1:0): 00 Linear, 01 4-beat wrap, 10 8-beat wrap, 11 16-beat wrap.
For description languages that allow default values for input ports (like VHDL), [CTI_I()] MAY be assigned a default value of '000'.
